rationale: Block 8 covers systematic quadrant-by-quadrant TM examination. This question tests understanding of the quadrant-based approach and its clinical relevance, anchoring to the oto-microscopic examination technique.

Block 11 covers interpretation of oto-microscopic findings including the safe/unsafe CSOM distinction. A TrueFalse statement encoding this known-trap (safe CSOM = tubotympanic, pars tensa central perforation with no cholesteatoma) reinforces the critical clinical rule.

Block 9 covers interpretation of DNE findings. The laterality rule for nasal polyps is a critical EN known-trap: bilateral polyps suggest inflammatory/allergic disease, while a unilateral polyp must raise suspicion of neoplasia until proven otherwise.

Block 7 covers the three-pass systematic survey of DNE. This question tests application of the three-pass technique, requiring the student to identify what is visualised in each pass — a direct procedural knowledge check.

Block 9 covers interpretation of laryngoscopic findings. A question differentiating glottic from supraglottic carcinoma applies the EN known-trap on laryngeal subsites and their distinct clinical and prognostic implications.
Block 3 covers indications for laryngoscopy. The three-week hoarseness rule is a critical EN known-trap and a mandatory referral threshold that all final-year students must recall automatically.
